property_summary: After deploying the contract, admin (deployer) calls setOwner(alice). On reference, owner updates to alice; on buggy version, owner does not change (remains deployer).

After admin sets owner to a new address via setOwner, the reference version sets owner to the new address, while the buggy version sets owner to address(0); the test checks that owner is the new address.

After deploying, the admin (the original deployer) calls setOwner(0x...), which sets owner to the caller in the reference but to the contract's balance payer (msg.sender) in the modified version; reading owner shows the admin in reference and a different address in the modified version.
After admin calls setOwner, the reference returns true while the buggy version returns false, causing an assertion on the return value to fail.

After calling setOwner as admin, onlyAdmin modifier should not revert on the second call; the reference permits calling a public view after setOwner, but the buggy version's duplicated require in onlyAdmin reverts on the second invocation.

After a non-admin calls setOwner multiple times, the reference allows it because onlyAdmin allows calls from msg.sender (the deployer) while the buggy version rejects due to duplicate require that prevents the state change from persisting; concretely, the owner becomes the non-admin in the reference but stays the original owner in the buggy version.

The admin sets the owner via setOwner, then the non-admin tries to call setOwner; the reference version allows the admin to set the owner and rejects non-admin, while the buggy version repeats the onlyAdmin check after the function body causing the modifier to revert for non-admin as expected, but the assertion focuses on the admin being able to successfully set the owner—the reference correctly returns true, whereas the buggy version reverts when admin calls setOwner due to the extra require statement in the modifier.

After the owner is set via setOwner, the second version (which repeats the onlyAdmin check after the function body) reverts when calling setOwner a second time because the check is evaluated again after the function has already executed, causing a reversion of the second call, while the reference version allows it.

After a non-admin calls setOwner, the reference sets the owner (the assertion passes), while the buggy version reverts due to the duplicated require in the onlyAdmin modifier (the assertion fails because the call reverts).

In the reference version, only the admin can call setOwner, so a non-admin call will revert; in the buggy version the modifier is empty, so a non-admin can successfully change the owner, and the assertion that a non-admin call reverts breaks.
After deployment, the reference version sets owner to msg.sender, while the bug sets owner to address(0); the test asserts that owner equals the deployer.

After deploying C, the owner is set twice in the buggy version. Reading c.owner() shows the admin address in the reference, but the buggy version returns address(0) because the second assignment overwrites to payable(msg.sender) which is address(0) during deployment.
Calling setOwner by the admin fails on the reference but reverts on the buggy version because the buggy constructor sets owner twice, making the onlyAdmin modifier check fail.

After constructor, reading owner returns the admin twice in the buggy version (the last assignment in constructor overrides the first), so the invariant that owner == admin is broken only in the buggy version.

The reference constructor sets owner once to the deployer, but the modified constructor sets owner twice, which is idempotent, so the test checks that owner equals the deployer; both versions satisfy this, so this property is not divergent.

After deploying the contract, calling setOwner with a non-owner admin should succeed; the reference version allows the call, but the second version reverts due to an extra onlyOwner modifier requirement.

After a non-admin calls setOwner, the second version's onlyOwner modifier double-checks the same require, which doesn't change behavior, so the test assertion checks that onlyAdmin correctly blocks non-admin calls.

After calling setOwner with a non-admin, in REFERENCE the owner stays unchanged, but in second version the modifier executes its repeated require twice causing a revert, so c.owner() equals the original owner in REFERENCE but is unreachable in second version.

After calling setOwner to change owner to a different address, the onlyOwner modifier on a view function should not revert; the reference allows the call, but the second version has an extra require that makes it revert because the second require fails when msg.sender matches owner.
